topic.name: The Area of a General Triangle

question.text: The area of ​​the triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $\dfrac{15\sqrt{3}}{2} \text{ cm}^2.$ Determine $m \angle A.$
question.explanation:
The formula for the area of the triangle is \[ \mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}bc\sin{A}, \] where $\angle{A}$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$

Here, we have \begin{align*} c & = AB = 5 \text{ cm},\\ b & = AC = 6 \text{ cm}. \end{align*}

Therefore, we can calculate $m\angle A$ as follows:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} \mathcal{A} & = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot b \cdot c \cdot \sin A\\[5pt] \dfrac{15\sqrt{3}}{2} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 5 \cdot 6 \cdot \sin{A}\\[5pt] \dfrac{15\sqrt{3}}{2} & = 15 \cdot \sin{A}\\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{15}\sqrt{3}}{2} & = \cancel{15} \cdot \sin{A}\\[5pt] \sin{A} & = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\\[5pt] m\angle A & = 60^\circ. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating an Angle or Side of a Triangle Given the Area of a Triangle

question.text: Rounded to the nearest tenth, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
question.explanation:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle BDC$ (see the illustration below).

First we find the area for $\triangle ABD\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{ABD} &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 6 \cdot 10 \cdot \sin 110^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 30 \cdot \sin 110^\circ\\[5pt] &\approx 28.190\,7, \end{align*} rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area for $\triangle BCD\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{BDC} &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 13 \cdot 15 \cdot \sin 58^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 97.5 \cdot \sin 58^\circ \\[5pt] &\approx 82.684\,7, \end{align*} rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} &= \mathcal{A}_{ABD}+\mathcal{A}_{BDC} \\ &= 28.190\,7 + 82.684\,7\\ &= 110.875\,4 \end{align*}

Consequently, to the nearest tenth, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $110.9.$

example.title: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.text: The area of $ABCD$ is $34 \text{ cm}^2.$ What is the area of $\triangle BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?
question.explanation:
Let's start by finding the area of $\triangle ABD.$ We get

\begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} & =\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot AB \cdot AD \cdot \sin{A}\\[5pt] &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 9 \cdot 15 \cdot \sin 52^ \circ \\[5pt] &=67.5 \cdot \sin 52^\circ \\[5pt] & = 53.190 \ldots\\[5pt] & \approx 53 \textrm{ cm}^2 \end{align*} rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of $\triangle ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $\triangle BCD.$ Therefore, \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle BCD} & = \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} - \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} \\[2pt] & = 53 - 34 \\[2pt] & = 19 \textrm{ cm}^2. \end{align*}
